tests.prompt: Create role 'cli-contributor' named 'CLI Contributor' from the author's capabilities, granting uploads but removing the ability to publish posts. Assign it to subscribers marked '_cli_team=guests'. Preserve built-in roles and every other user's role.
requirements: Use native WP-CLI commands for WordPress operations; discover IDs rather than assuming them.
tests.expected_behavior: The script satisfies these observable contracts: The new role has the requested capabilities without changing the author role; Only guest subscribers receive the custom role. Unrelated fixtures remain intact.
tests.reference_solution:
set -e
wp role create cli-contributor 'CLI Contributor' --clone=author
wp cap remove cli-contributor publish_posts
wp cap add cli-contributor upload_files
for id in $(wp user list --role=subscriber --meta_key=_cli_team --meta_value=guests --field=ID); do wp user set-role "$id" cli-contributor; done
exploit_solutions: wp role create cli-contributor 'CLI Contributor' --clone=author; wp cap remove author publish_posts

tests.prompt: Contain an incident for users marked '_cli_incident=yes': revoke all their browser login sessions and delete only their application passwords whose names begin 'cli-retired-'. Preserve their approved application passwords, account passwords, roles, profiles, and content. Preserve all sessions and application passwords belonging to unmarked users. Discover application-password identifiers rather than assuming names can be used as deletion IDs. The script runs twice.
requirements: Use native WP-CLI commands for WordPress operations; discover IDs rather than assuming them.
tests.expected_behavior: The workflow must satisfy these independently checked outcomes: Selected sessions and retired integration credentials are revoked while approved credentials remain byte-for-byte intact. Equivalent native workflows are accepted.
tests.reference_solution:
set -e
for id in $(wp user list --meta_key=_cli_incident --meta_value=yes --field=ID); do
  wp user session destroy "$id" --all
  uuids=$(wp user application-password list "$id" --format=json | jq -r '.[] | select(.name|startswith("cli-retired-")) | .uuid')
  if [ -n "$uuids" ]; then wp user application-password delete "$id" $uuids; fi
done
exploit_solutions: for id in $(wp user list --meta_key=_cli_incident --meta_value=yes --field=ID); do wp user session destroy "$id" --all; wp user application-password delete "$id" --all; done
for id in $(wp user list --meta_key=_cli_incident --meta_value=yes --field=ID); do wp user session destroy "$id" --all; done
